The barometric pressure drops, or the first firework cracks, or you just pick up your keys — and something in your dog changes. The pacing starts. The panting. Some dogs try to fold themselves into the smallest space they can find: behind the toilet, under the bed, in the shower stall. Others chew at a doorframe or claw at a crate trying to get to you.

You call their name and it doesn't quite land. You sit on the floor with them and it helps, some — until you have to get up. That's the specific kind of helpless this vest was made for. Not to fix the storm. Just to give your dog something steady to lean on when you can't be the one holding them.

The mechanism, honestly explained

Why gentle pressure helps at all.

The idea behind Furvago isn't new or complicated: steady, even pressure has a long, well-understood history of helping calm an anxious body — it's the same principle behind swaddling a newborn or wrapping up in a weighted blanket. The vest wraps snugly around your dog's chest and torso and stays there, applying that same gentle, constant pressure for as long as it's on.

Many dog owners report their dogs settle faster, pace less, and seem more comfortable with it on — especially during storms, fireworks, and time alone. It isn't a sedative, and it isn't a cure. We haven't run a clinical trial and we won't pretend we have. For some dogs, it's a small help. For a lot of dogs, it becomes part of the routine on the nights that are hardest.

If your dog's anxiety is severe, or you're not seeing any difference after several tries, that's worth a conversation with your vet — the vest is meant to sit alongside good veterinary care, not replace it.

In practice

How to put it on — and when.

1

Slide it over their head

Let the collar opening rest naturally at the base of the neck.

Under a minute
2

Wrap and fasten

Snug but not tight — you should be able to slip two flat fingers underneath.

Two-finger fit
3

Time it right

When you can, put it on 15–20 minutes before a trigger you know is coming.

15–20 min early
4

Leave it on as needed

Most owners remove it once the storm passes or once they're back home.

Until they're settled

Three minutes of prep, and they're ready for whatever's coming.

What to expect

It's not always instant.

Some dogs settle within the first few minutes: a lowered tail, slower breathing, lying down instead of pacing. Others need two or three wears before they stop noticing the vest is even there and start associating it with the calm that follows. A small number of dogs don't respond much at all — that's a real, honest possibility, and not every dog reacts to gentle pressure the same way.

  • A tail that drops and softens

    Instead of staying tucked or stiff.

    First sign of calm

  • Breathing that slows

    Or a sigh as they settle into lying down.

    Settling in

  • Choosing to lie near you

    Instead of pacing or hiding.

    Fully at ease

If your dog seems more distressed in the vest — not less — take it off and talk to your vet before trying again.

Every dog settles differently — but they don't have to do it alone.

Our story

We built this on a bad thunderstorm night.

Furvago started with one dog, one storm, and the awful feeling of not being able to help.

The night that started it.

There's a specific kind of helplessness in watching your dog come apart during a storm — the shaking, the panting, the way they press into you like you're the only solid thing left. You hold them, and it helps a little, until you have to let go.

We went looking for something that could keep holding them when we couldn't. What we found was the simple, well-understood idea that gentle, steady pressure can calm an anxious body. So we set out to make a vest around it — one that fits properly, goes on easily, and is soft enough to wear through a whole bad night.

Furvago is a small brand with a narrow focus: help dogs feel safe when the world feels like too much. That's the whole mission. No miracle claims — just a thoughtful thing that has helped a lot of dogs settle.

Some nights, they just need to be held a little longer than you can manage.

Questions & answers

The things owners actually ask us.

Honest answers about how the vest works, sizing, and getting it to your door.

Honestly? It depends on the dog. Gentle, constant pressure has a long history of helping with anxiety — it's the same idea as swaddling a baby or using a weighted blanket — and many owners tell us their dogs settle faster and rest more easily with it on. It isn't a cure, and it isn't a substitute for veterinary care if your dog's anxiety is severe. For some dogs it's a small help; for many, it becomes part of the routine on stormy nights.

Ideally before the stressful moment starts — as a storm rolls in, before fireworks begin, or a little while before you leave the house. Giving your dog a chance to relax into it beforehand tends to work better than waiting until they're already panicking.

Measure the widest part of your dog's chest (just behind the front legs) and check it against the size guide on the product page. If your dog is between sizes, size up for a comfortable fit. Note: final measurements are being confirmed and will be updated before launch.

It's designed to be comfortable enough to wear through a storm or an evening of fireworks. As with anything your dog wears, check that the fit is snug but not tight, make sure they can move and breathe easily, and take it off for sleep and unsupervised time.

The vest works through gentle pressure alone — no medication, no scents, nothing your dog ingests. Always supervise your dog while they're wearing it, and if your dog has severe anxiety or a medical condition, talk to your vet about the best approach. Furvago is meant to complement that care, not replace it.
